name: Joshua
overview: Joshua was a male figure known as the Beth-shemite, a designation that identifies his origin or association as noted in 1 Samuel 6:14. No tribe or additional personal details are recorded about him. His role and significance are primarily understood through his unique attribute and biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Joshua means 'y-h-v-h saves,' reflecting a divine aspect of salvation associated with his identity. This proper name, mentioned in 1 Samuel 6:14, highlights the theological significance embedded in his name without indicating it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Joshua beyond his unique attribute as the Beth-shemite. There are no listed relationships or familial connections documented in the given information.
scriptureSignificance: Joshua's importance in Scripture is rooted in his leadership of Israel following Moses' death, guiding the people into the Promised Land. His faithfulness as one of the twelve spies who trusted God's promise, along with his role in the conquest of Canaan, marks him as a key figure of obedience and trust in God's salvation. His name and actions prefigure Christ, who leads believers into their spiritual inheritance and rest.
